notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #10] Video Tour and Demo coming soon
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

Let's start with an important announcement: this year we'll release the first Demo of Glasshouse on Steam. Due to circumstances beyond our control, we can't reveal the date yet -- just know that we've almost completed work on ACT I and this demo will be taken directly from a portion of it.

Now comes the most exciting part of development; we're implementing dialogues, assets, and mechanics, and what once seemed like an impossible puzzle to complete is now a wonderful interactive canvas. We want to celebrate GLASSHOUSE's 3rd birthday with a video tour of Dormitory 73B, one of the main settings, now finally connected between almost all its parts.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/d1e1b6b5ab46e4cb099e76d84f4b27b1eb1ed25c.gif

SHARED SPACES: FROM GROUND FLOOR TO 3RD FLOOR
Dormitory 73B consists of four floors and six apartments; its past as an industrial slaughterhouse has allowed us to build an intricate and unpredictable level design, architecturally 'uncomfortable' and full of secrets to discover. Each apartment is completely explorable and directly mirrors the popular culture of the Lundonstoch fiefdom.

[previewyoutube=NYl34ZgMIE4;full][/previewyoutube]
While waiting to reveal more information about the Demo's release date, in the coming months we'll begin to show you in detail all the pillars that make up the definitive GLASSHOUSE experience, from the Combat System to the Political Compass, including a complete overhaul of the UI itself.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/8f01e4c5d1e49e36aa367ee60c585f3b09903d20.gif

Since the release of the Concept Demo in 2023, we've been working tirelessly for over two years to reach this point -- 2025 is the year when Glasshouse will show itself in its definitive form: new trailer, public demo, press releases, rebranding (new logo coming!), a series of YouTube Devlogs and much more awaits you in this new phase of collective development.

In case you're wondering, no, we still haven't found funding and work continues in our free time as it did in 2022. But as was the case three years ago, the flame that fuels our passion remains strong and with or without a publisher, we will see this through to the end. That's a promise.

Thank you all, see you next month!

Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #9] Visual Upgrades
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

I'm Andrea Marinelli, Lead Technical Artist at FLAT28, and I am temporarily ousting Giacomo to create my first devblog. A techno-junkie one.

Over the past few months, we’ve been focusing heavily on improving the visual side of Glasshouse. Our goal has been twofold: to define a clear visual identity and to set a benchmark for visual quality—a standard we aim to hit with every environment in the game.

To achieve that, we’ve been moving forward on multiple fronts. On one side, we kept working on new assets and building out the Dormitory 73B scenarios to maintain production momentum. On the other, we explored new pipelines to speed up development while increasing overall visual fidelity.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/83d83d06a493328c7ba9f7498d71942dd224b69d.gif

CLEANER EDGES & ROOM BORDERS
We’ve reworked the borders of every room and apartment in Dormitory 73B. The goal was to get a softer, more natural separation between the interior and exterior parts of the rooms, while staying consistent with the aesthetic we're aiming for. The result feels more polished, cohesive, and true to our vision.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/5635922b37ff8dfef08443c5bf541d9268c547c3.gif

NEW POST-PROCESSING & OUTLINES
One of the changes we're most excited about—and one you’ll likely notice right away—is a new post-processing effect that adds subtle outlines across the entire scene. (well, might be actually tricky to get it via gif)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/8a7b1b0ab7df3bf241f5757bfd74bc807c44c4e8.gif

After testing various styles, we landed on an outline shader that felt just right for the tone and identity of Glasshouse. Both the characters and environments now have a light contour that enhances detail and brings out the uniqueness of our art direction.

From an isometric top-down view, this effect also makes small details more readable, giving players a clearer and sharper sense of space and depth.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7574251189c05e645cd3c7fa583ef1118b82d4c1.gif

CLOTH SIMULATION
Until now, most of the cloth elements—curtains, drapes, and similar—were entirely static. That’s changing. We’ve begun integrating real-time cloth simulation for selected elements.

Not all fabrics in the game will be dynamic, due to both performance considerations and artistic direction. But certain curtains and fabrics will now react to player interaction—swaying, shifting, or sliding over characters as they move through them. It’s a small touch, but it adds a sense of life and responsiveness to the environments.

DLSS & UPSCALING EXPERIMENTS

While it’s still early to talk in-depth about optimization, we’ve started preparing for it. Glasshouse already supports NVIDIA DLSS 3 internally, and we’re exploring dynamic resolution scaling and other upscaling techniques to ensure smooth performance across a wide range of hardware.

That’s all for now—but more is coming. We can’t wait to show you what’s next.

Andrea Marinelli, Lead Technical Artist
FLAT28 Collective

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #8] Designing the perfect lockdown-story setting
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,  

today we bring you an update on the progress of the main setting of Glasshouse, Dormitory 73B — and perhaps also a small reflection on the architectural philosophy behind it.  

The compromise of privacy, inside and outside the lockdown.  

There isn’t a single member of FLAT28 who hasn’t lived outside of a condominium complex. Our entire lives, up until now, have always revolved around waiting for a crowded elevator that would never arrive, and that’s exactly where we started: war in private spaces, coexistence in shared spaces.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/155e251d70344365e3bc008a6b2690809a1f9991.jpg  

GROUND FLOOR [GF]  
After a long day of work, you enter the lobby, and the number of piled-up trash is only surpassed by the chaotic tangle of notes plastered on the walls. "This place is not a dump / Taps will stop running water from 08:00 to 18:00 / The elevator is broken, call the technician."  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/c441f4907e2522fb45e5900be2a9c6d3f5136fc5.png  

The Dormitory 73B is the perfect embodiment of this scenario, amplified beyond measure by the lockdown conditions that the residents of the Lundonstoch fiefdom have endured for over 57 days. At first glance, the ground floor of this condominium is cold and unwelcoming. The pale color of the concrete is almost blinding, and the dense network of pipes weaves its way into private properties, forming a noose around the necks of those who live there.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/a008ad634c28b22d6a0cb8de9fd7db5b2605a864.png  

During the early 1900s, the Grand Council of Lundonstoch promoted a collectivization effort aimed at redeveloping old private factories into condominium complexes. Here, the industrial violently clashes with the residential — as if to remind us that we are all cogs in the great machine.  

There are no windows; they are not functional.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/3f8906bf19b6fd16080b9eff3b304712cb4176e5.jpg  

SECOND FLOOR [2F]  
Each landing hosts two apartments, typically two-room units. The walls prefer to extend in height rather than width. The warm morning light filtering through the glass panels has turned this floor into a small living room where neighbors gather for tea before heading to work.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/28525a716a2ce116c696b0de06b40eb4ba0a53dd.gif  

The goal was to banish the gray specter of the factory with furniture, rugs, and quilts. Although the management of shared spaces fell to the head-tenants, it had become common practice. In the Lundonstoch fiefdom, every dormitory was a micro-society within society itself.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/edafdb48d68b7a8a9629f7307095b6b824976ebc.png  

The rules were established by the head-tenant in charge through the "Condominium Constitution" and could only be challenged by the arm of the fiefdom, the vassals of the Damage Control Brigade (DCB), the authority.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/d16a5f07cb07aac6ed26d70b236e575f0e6c73d1.png  

TECHNOLOGY  
For over 300 years, Lundonstoch relied on Peat Power Plants, an organic material formed from the partial decomposition of vegetation in waterlogged, acidic environments like marshes and moors.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/fcff1e340b79770a08b8d9096bd456e78845629c.png  

When a study in the 1980s revealed that the average life expectancy had dropped to 65 years and that infertility had reached 70% of the population, the Grand Feudal Council decided to implement a new, more efficient and less harmful system: coal.  

With the support of Devs from the fiefdom of Ørstedia, Gravity Furnaces were quickly designed and distributed to all dormitories, leading to the temporary closure of all underground energy networks (Old Lundonstoch Canals) due to obsolescence.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/ca632db5732933a998c8679a49f7c974043de747.png  

This energy decentralization operation effectively gave each dormitory a cumbersome heart, a maintenance room accessible only to the fiefdom’s technical operators. No tenant had access to it, not even the head-tenant.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f622ee2c91f9389113b2546631fe1edd0f5cb0e6.jpg  

The one adapted in Glasshouse, as you can see, is an inductive Narrative Design that starts from the micro to better understand the macro. Private property is nothing more than a small window into the vast society of The World of Glass.  

We are a small team, we couldn’t afford to create an open world, so we rolled up our sleeves and drew from what we know best: thin air, crumbling corridors, and small rooms/spaces overflowing with stories. When COVID-19 forced us into our condominiums for months, it wasn’t a huge tragedy — we already had everything we needed, our small self-governed ecosystem.  

Thank you all, see you next month!  

Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director  
FLAT28 Collective

notes.title: GLASSHOUSE - FAQ #1
notes.content:
Hello flatmates!

In light of recent updates, many questions have arisen about Glasshouse and its future, so we want to take the opportunity to put together a handy FAQ and get ready for 2025, a year that will hold many surprises.

So, let's get into it!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/3f2958fd6db8b3057e89946da2730d08d2ad32e0.gif

Q: What is Glasshouse?
A: Glasshouse is an isometric Turn-Based-CRPG set in a post-capitalist feudalpunk world at the dawn of a terrible world war. Inspired by RPGs such as Disco Elysium and Pathologic, Glasshouse promises an intense narrative-roleplaying experience punctuated by unforgettable characters, complex dialogue trees, multiple endings and deep ideological introspections that go beyond the screen.

Q: What's the Plot of Glasshouse?
A: The entire fiefdom is in lockdown when a mysterious triple murder occurs in your apartment building. Unknowingly, you are caught up in a political conspiracy bigger than yourself. Find a way out or find yourself.

Q: Who is the developer FLAT28?
A: We are an international art collective consisting of 17 members from the film, CGI and video game industries. We have been working on Glasshouse since 2022 in our spare time, without salaries, funding or publishers. Completely smart working.

Q: What's Feudalpunk?
A: Feudalpunk is a fictional subgenre that mixes elements of the feudal era with contemporary themes or technologies, focusing on social themes such as class struggle and the sharp contrast between them. In Glasshouse's post-capitalist world, following the revolution of 1828, the geopolitical order has overthrown the state model in favour of the democratic feudal model. Inspired by the Kurdish manifesto of Democratic Confederalism, Glasshouse imagines a deglobalised world where technological progress has come to a standstill and the economic-social gap between fiefdoms is unbridgeable, where 100km distance between one fiefdom and another can be equivalent to 100 years of technological difference.

Q: Does Glasshouse have a combat system?
A: Yes, as announced a few months ago, Glasshouse will have turn-based combat inspired by older Final Fantasy and the more recent Fear & Hunger.

Q: When is the Release Date?
A: Too early to announce it.

Q: Are you planning an Early Access Release?
A: No, no early access release is currently planned.

Q: Are you planning a Kickstarter campaign?
A: It depends on many factors, first and foremost, the general interest around Glasshouse in these early stages. Kickstarter has changed over time and a proper campaign may require a lot of funding, which we currently do not have.

Q: Will there be voice acting?
A: The aim is to have Glasshouse, for the launch, at least with partial voice acting. To date, as there is no publisher, it is difficult to say for sure.

Q: How long will Glasshouse be?
A: We expect to have a main campaign between 10 and 15 hours. We are a small team (without budget) and want to create a strong, intense and highly replayable experience. For our ambitions, it is necessary to reduce the duration to have an rpg component that really makes a difference. 

Q: Are there any DLC planned?
A: We have at least one expansion of the main story in mind, but nothing is certain. It will depend a lot on how the development of Glasshouse proceeds and on sales. Let's be clear, we are not talking about cut content, but a possible small additional story that will give another point of view to the main plot.

Q: What is the Concept Demo of Glasshouse?
A: A small 3-hour standalone experience from the first 2022 builds of Glasshouse, when we were young and didn't yet know what we were doing. It is a vertical slice mainly designed to sell the settings, atmospheres and core game mechanics to publishers. Nothing included in the concept demo will be present in the final Glasshouse game. You can download it from Itch.io.

Q: Why was the Concept Demo removed from Steam?
A: It was originally conceived in 2022 for pitching to Publishers, and later adapted to a wider audience to gather feedback, experiment and fine-tune our production pipeline. Now, two years later, this version no longer represents the final product and for this reason, we have decided to remove it.

Q: Will the game be available on GOG and other stores?
A: It’ll likely be available on GOG and EPIC Store.

Q: Will preorders be available?
A: No. ♥♥♥♥ preorders.

Q: What platforms other than PC are planned for release?
A: We’re planning releases for PS5 and Xbox S/X, likely following the PC release.

Q: What engine is the game being developed in?
A: Unity.

Q: How can I get in touch with the devs?
A: You can write us at prj.glasshouse@gmail.com or join our  Discord .

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7493d54596c091c2cb1ffb076071f102d3eddaed.gif

That's it for this year, and I want to take this space to make a promise: from 2025 onwards you can expect a devblog every month, with the aim of offering an ever-expanding window on the stormy development journey of the FLAT28 collective. Making video games isn't easy, but damn if it's fun.

We can't wait to reveal the future of Glasshouse to you.

Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #2] The Art of Glasshouse
notes.content:
Hello humans,

In this dev blog we'd like to tell you about the philosophy behind the making of one of our protagonists, Dormitory73B, the setting for Glasshouse!

FLAT28 is a collective of about 20 people who, during our spare time, set out to tell the story of a proletarian community in a new society, a new world. Given the big elephant in the room (lack of any kind of budget), it was immediately clear that an open world formula would never work.

How to deal with the harsh reality accordingly?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/1f0a4e4f2d24aff7e583d3a07f9c5ab4357ce9fd.gif


 Our approach has been to work in the small context. Private property is an honest mirror of society. The furnishing of a flat or its architecture are not just goods, but can be a means of storytelling.


Often in cRPGs interiors are just a point B between the journey from A to B, in Glasshouse the apartment building is all that is left of a society in the throes of a nuclear revolution.
Wealdmaer, the player, finds himself in a lockdown situation forced by events he cannot escape.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/195b2b07cb9876e49a2a3628028478464710b232.png


 We therefore took inspiration from the giants creators of closed worlds such as Resident Evil and Haunting Ground, gaming experiences that were able to build a complex and intricate level design from a single building.


Dormitory 73B is a privileged opportunity to get to know and touch the private sphere of Lundonstoch Feud society. The apartment building will provide unprecedented stimuli for exploration, between shared residential spaces and private flats.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/f00751ab11d7d771ea3ad826c22bbb9659f02341.png


 Apartment 28 is the central hub of Glasshouse, the home of the protagonist and his housemates, Ecgberth and Voitsehk. Two floors in which to interact with each small asset in order to obtain resources useful for survival or progress in the main story.


In Glasshouse, the exploration of the containers does not stop at the simple "click > drag > drop" but presents a system in which textual exploration can turn out to be a labyrinth of options that conceal unprecedented interactions. For instance, a seemingly innocuous bookcase could hide secret compartments or the structure itself could be deprived of components such as nails and wood, useful for crafting.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/672246ca1c30fa5ed0f1713bb3ab317f9d8837df.jpg


 Like a Matryoshka doll, in fact, the architecture and furniture of Dormitory 73B can offer different levels of interaction at various times during the main quest, whether it be dialogue options unlocked by certain tools or codes for suitcases belonging abandoned by past housemates.


Each polygonal model has a story to tell (literally, inanimate objects can talk to you and are in fact NPCs with personalities, but that's another story) and is a founding part of the world building of a post-capitalist society where privatisation is at historical limits.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/bf94110713b5e9ae8737cdc20fc4e1f1bd20ad47.gif

That is why we also decided to make the isometric view closer, we want the player to be able to perceive time and space better. In Glasshouse, the camera can abandon the isometric view to immerse the player even more in the nooks and crannies of the apartment building. The change of perspective as a game philosophy, both in form and content!


Thank you so much, that's all for today, see ya next time!

Giacomo Montagnoli, Game Director
FLAT28 Collective
